biography.plain_text: Alexander Miliavsky is a Russian businessman and former Moscow City Duma deputy. Born in Minsk, he built a substantial property business around the Rubin television plant, converting industrial premises into the Gorbushkin Dvor shopping centre. His interests expanded into residential and commercial development before the sale of major retail assets.

confidence.reason: Primary interview and independent business reporting establish the identity, formation and property development; contemporary resignation reporting confirms that the public office is former.

biography.html: Alexander Miliavsky is a Russian businessman and former Moscow City Duma deputy. Born in Minsk, he built a substantial property business around the Rubin television plant, converting industrial premises into the Gorbushkin Dvor shopping centre. His interests expanded into residential and commercial development before the sale of major retail assets.

long_biography.plain_text:
Russian businessman Alexander Miliavsky learned to maintain seismic-survey equipment while working in the Yamal-Nenets region. After qualifying as an electronics engineer, he serviced recording stations and vehicles carrying vibration equipment for oil and gas exploration. Further training in France gave him certification to install and service sophisticated equipment made by CGG.

That technical background informed his work at Rubin. He regarded the Moscow factory's irregular, multistorey layout as an obstacle to modern production, compounded by high labour costs. The company shifted television assembly to the Videofon plant in Voronezh, installing automated systems and bringing together Russian and Belarusian engineers to develop its products.

confidence.reason: His detailed first-person interview directly supports the technical work, French training and factory decisions. Independent contemporary reporting corroborates the production relocation. Self-promotional claims about world-leading quality are omitted.
